messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- INC-2025-004 was an incident affecting the notifier on 2025-02-06. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- INC-2025-023 was an incident affecting the indexer on 2025-10-13. [valid 2025-10-16 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-023]
- INC-2025-017 was an incident affecting the auth gateway on 2025-07-27. [valid 2025-08-01 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-017]
- The root cause of INC-2026-003 was a retry loop that ignored idempotency keys. [valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- INC-2026-009 was an incident in which the scheduler ran the nightly jobs twice on 2026-05-03. [valid 2026-05-08 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-009]
- INC-2026-003 was an incident in which the webhooks service delivered some events twice on 2026-01-17. [valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- INC-2025-011 was caused by an index missing after the schema migration. [valid 2025-04-28 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-011]
- The root cause of INC-2025-023 was a reindex job that failed silently on a full disk, leaving stale results for two days. [valid 2025-10-16 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-023]
- INC-2025-017's root cause was an expired intermediate certificate, which took logins down. [valid 2025-08-01 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-017]
- Priya runs the quarterly capacity review. [valid 2025-06-23 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-06-23]
- Oskar runs the weekly architecture review. [valid 2026-06-16 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-06-16]
- The monthly cost review is run by Yuki. [valid 2025-10-13 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-10-13]
- On 2025-08-01, it was decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead. [decision; valid 2025-08-01 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-017]
- During INC-2025-011, the ledger saw write latency spike tenfold for an hour on 2025-04-26. [valid 2025-04-28 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-011]
- INC-2026-009 happened because two leaders were elected on the scheduler during a network partition. [valid 2026-05-08 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-009]
- Team Dune decided the webhooks service will sign payloads with rotating keys because a partner asked for key rotation in their security review. [valid 2025-10-22 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-10-22]
- During INC-2025-004, a stuck offset went unnoticed for 40 minutes. [valid 2025-02-11 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2025-004]
- The notifier's flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages. [valid 2025-02-20 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-20]
- On 2026-01-22, the team decided the webhooks service will require an idempotency key on every delivery, because the duplicate deliveries in INC-2026-003 came from retries without one. [decision; valid 2026-01-22 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]

Question: On what date was the review of INC-2025-004 written?
